props.doc:
SIEM and log platforms: the ingestion side of the estate.

A SIEM observes and correlates; it does not contain. Every command here is
read-only except for updating an incident back in the vendor console, which
is how an analyst working in the SIEM sees what the SOAR did.

Each pack also declares a `poll` block: the query the ingest role runs on a
schedule to pull new alerts, and the field that carries the watermark.
props.name: siem_connectors

props.code:
def param(kind, **extra):
    """One input property, in JSON Schema terms."""
    spec = {"type": kind} if kind not in ("ipv4", "hostname") else {"type": "string"}
    spec.update(extra)
    return spec


def cmd(key, name, method, url, inputs, outputs, extract=None, risk="low",
        effect="read", doc="", techniques=None, undo=None, timeout_ms=30000,
        required=None, category="integration", body=None, success=None):
    """
    One command definition.

    Structured JSON in, structured JSON out. The output_schema is what the
    playbook validator type-checks the next step against, so a command whose
    schema lies fails at publish rather than at 03:00.
    """
    definition = {
        "key": key,
        "name": name,
        "category": category,
        "kind": "http",
        "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "required": list(inputs.keys()) if required is None else required,
            "properties": inputs,
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
        "output_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": outputs},
        "implementation": {
            "method": method,
            "url": url,
            "extract": extract or {},
            "success_codes": success or [200, 201, 202, 204],
        },
        "required_permissions": ["commands.execute"],
        "required_capabilities": ["net"],
        "timeout_ms": timeout_ms,
        "risk_level": risk,
        "effect": effect,
        "trust_level": "trusted",
        "technique_ids": techniques or [],
        "doc": doc,
    }
    if body is not None:
        definition["implementation"]["body"] = body
    if effect == "mutating":
        # A mutating command with no dry-run example would make dry run a lie,
        # and the registry validator refuses it.
        definition["dry_run_example"] = {"dry_run": True, "would_call": key}
    if undo:
        # Named, not inferred. The platform never invents a rollback.
        definition["undo_command"] = undo
    if risk == "high":
        definition["required_permissions"] = ["commands.execute", _permission_for(key)]
    return definition


def _permission_for(key):
    """High-risk commands need the response permission that matches them."""
    action = key.split(".", 1)[1]
    if "isolate" in action or "contain" in action or "quarantine_host" in action:
        return "response.isolate"
    if "block" in action:
        return "response.block"
    if "disable" in action or "suspend" in action:
        return "response.disable_account"
    if "revoke" in action or "signout" in action:
        return "response.revoke_sessions"
    if "delete" in action or "purge" in action or "remove_mail" in action:
        return "response.delete_mail"
    if "firewall" in action or "policy" in action:
        return "response.firewall"
    return "response.isolate"


def field(name, label, kind="text", required=True, default=None,
          options=None, help="", placeholder=""):
    # One thing an operator must be told before this tool can be reached.
    return {
        "name": name, "label": label, "kind": kind, "required": required,
        "default": default, "options": options or [], "help": help,
        "placeholder": placeholder,
    }


def connector(cid, name, vendor, category, auth, base_url, allowlist, commands,
              min_permissions=None, rate_limit=None, health=None,
              version="1.0.0", setup=None, derive=None, ingest=None,
              hunt=None):
    # A connector manifest. Installing one publishes its commands; no engine
    # change.
    #
    # setup is what THIS vendor needs before it can be reached, and no two
    # agree: CrowdStrike wants a cloud region, Sentinel a tenant and a
    # workspace, Splunk a host and a port. Asking every connector for a
    # client id and a secret asked the two questions they happen to share
    # and none of the ones that make a connection work.
    fields = list(setup or [])

    # Which setting the commands of this connector actually read. Most say
    # base_url; a few front a protocol that is not HTTP and say gateway_url
    # instead, and asking those for a base_url nothing reads is how a form
    # grows a field that does nothing.
    setting = "base_url"
    if "{{" in base_url:
        inner = base_url.split("{{", 1)[1].split("}}", 1)[0].strip()
        setting = inner.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] if inner else "base_url"

    if not any(f["name"] == setting for f in fields):
        # Every connector can at least be pointed elsewhere: a regional
        # cloud, a tenant-specific host, an on-premise appliance.
        # A connector whose base_url is itself a template has no host until
        # someone supplies one, so there is nothing to prefill and the field
        # is the only way the connection can exist at all.
        templated = "{{" in base_url
        fields.insert(0, field(
            setting, "API base URL", kind="url",
            default=None if templated else base_url,
            help="Change for a regional cloud or an on-premise appliance."
                 if not templated else "The hostname this tenant answers on."))

    return {
        "setup": fields,
        # Settings a vendor addresses by a composite of the ones a person
        # can actually be asked for. Nobody knows their workspace ARM id;
        # everybody knows their subscription, resource group and workspace
        # name, and the id is those three in a fixed shape.
        "derive": derive or {},
        # How this product is polled for alerts: which command lists them,
        # which turns ids into objects, and where the timestamp lives that
        # the watermark advances to. A connector without it can still
        # receive a webhook; it just cannot be asked.
        "ingest": ingest or {},
        # Which command runs an arbitrary hunt query, what the query
        # parameter is called, and what language an engineer is writing.
        # A tool without this cannot be hunted in - which is most of them,
        # because a firewall is not a place you go looking.
        "hunt": hunt or {},
        "id": cid, "name": name, "vendor": vendor, "category": category,
        "version": version, "auth": auth, "base_url": base_url,
        "egress_allowlist": allowlist,
        "min_vendor_permissions": min_permissions or [],
        "rate_limit": rate_limit or {},
        "health_check": health or {},
        "commands": commands,
        "publisher": "master-soar",
        "signature": "",
    }


rows_out = {"rows": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}},
            "row_count": {"type": "integer"}}

sentinel = connector(
    "microsoft.sentinel", "Microsoft Sentinel", "Microsoft", "siem",
    {"kind": "oauth2_client", "roles": ["client_id", "client_secret"],
     "token_url": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{{ integration.config.tenant_id }}/oauth2/v2.0/token",
     "scope": "https://management.azure.com/.default"},
    "https://management.azure.com",
    ["management.azure.com", "login.microsoftonline.com", "api.loganalytics.io"],
    min_permissions=["Microsoft Sentinel Responder", "Log Analytics Reader"],
    health={"path": "/subscriptions?api-version=2020-01-01"},
    setup=[
        field("tenant_id", "Entra tenant id",
              placeholder="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"),
        field("subscription_id", "Subscription id"),
        field("resource_group", "Resource group"),
        field("workspace_name", "Log Analytics workspace"),
        field("workspace_id", "Workspace id (GUID)", required=False,
              help="Needed to run KQL against the workspace."),
    ],
    ingest={
        # OData, not FQL, and the incident list already carries the
        # detail - so no detail call, and one fewer round trip per
        # poll than the EDRs need.
        "list": {"command": "sentinel.list_incidents",
                 "output": "incidents",
                 "inputs": {
                     "filter": "properties/createdTimeUtc gt {since}",
                     "limit": 100}},
        "combine": " and ",
        "watermark": "$.properties.createdTimeUtc",
    },
    hunt={
        "command": "sentinel.run_query", "input": "query",
        "output": "rows", "language": "KQL",
        # Log Analytics takes the window as an ISO-8601 duration, so
        # the lookback an engineer set in hours is handed over as one
        # rather than pasted into the query text.
        "window_input": "timespan", "window_format": "PT{hours}H",
    },
    commands=[
        cmd("sentinel.run_query", "Sentinel: Run KQL Query", "POST",
            "https://api.loganalytics.io/v1/workspaces/{{ integration.config.workspace_id }}/query",
            {"query": param("string", maxLength=32768),
             "timespan": param("string", pattern="^P.*$")},
            rows_out, {"rows": "$.tables[0].rows"},
            required=["query"], timeout_ms=180000,
            body={"query": "{{ inputs.query }}", "timespan": "{{ inputs.timespan }}"},
            doc="The query travels as a parameter from a saved query or an approved AI draft. It is never string-built from alert content."),

        cmd("sentinel.list_incidents", "Sentinel: List Incidents", "GET",
            "https://management.azure.com/{{ integration.config.workspace_arm_id }}/providers/Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents?api-version=2023-02-01&$filter={{ inputs.filter | urlencode }}&$top={{ inputs.limit | default(50) }}",
            {"filter": param("string"), "limit": param("integer", maximum=1000)},
            {"incidents": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"incidents": "$.value"}, required=[],
            doc="The polling command the ingest role uses when a webhook is not available."),

        cmd("sentinel.get_incident", "Sentinel: Get Incident", "GET",
            "https://management.azure.com/{{ integration.config.workspace_arm_id }}/providers/Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents/{{ inputs.incident_id | urlencode }}?api-version=2023-02-01",
            {"incident_id": param("string")},
            {"title": {"type": "string"}, "severity": {"type": "string"},
             "status": {"type": "string"}, "owner": {"type": "string"}},
            {"title": "$.properties.title", "severity": "$.properties.severity",
             "status": "$.properties.status",
             "owner": "$.properties.owner.userPrincipalName"}),

        cmd("sentinel.get_entities", "Sentinel: Get Incident Entities", "POST",
            "https://management.azure.com/{{ integration.config.workspace_arm_id }}/providers/Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents/{{ inputs.incident_id | urlencode }}/entities?api-version=2023-02-01",
            {"incident_id": param("string")},
            {"entities": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"entities": "$.entities"}),

        cmd("sentinel.get_incident_alerts",
            "Sentinel: Get Incident Alerts", "POST",
            "https://management.azure.com/{{ integration.config.workspace_arm_id }}/providers/Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents/{{ inputs.incident_id | urlencode }}/alerts?api-version=2023-02-01",
            {"incident_id": param("string")},
            {"alerts": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"alerts": "$.value"},
            doc="An incident is a container; the alerts inside it carry the "
                "detection detail and the entities. Fetching the incident "
                "alone gives an analyst a title and nothing to work with."),

        cmd("sentinel.update_incident", "Sentinel: Update Incident", "PUT",
            "https://management.azure.com/{{ integration.config.workspace_arm_id }}/providers/Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents/{{ inputs.incident_id | urlencode }}?api-version=2023-02-01",
            {"incident_id": param("string"),
             "status": param("string", enum=["New", "Active", "Closed"]),
             "classification": param("string",
                 enum=["TruePositive", "BenignPositive", "FalsePositive",
                       "Undetermined"]),
             "comment": param("string", maxLength=4000)},
            {"status": {"type": "string"}}, {"status": "$.properties.status"},
            risk="medium", effect="mutating", required=["incident_id", "status"],
            body={"properties": {"status": "{{ inputs.status }}",
                                 "classification": "{{ inputs.classification }}",
                                 "title": "{{ incident.title }}",
                                 "severity": "{{ incident.severity }}"}}),

        cmd("sentinel.add_comment", "Sentinel: Add Incident Comment", "PUT",
            "https://management.azure.com/{{ integration.config.workspace_arm_id }}/providers/Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents/{{ inputs.incident_id | urlencode }}/comments/{{ inputs.comment_id }}?api-version=2023-02-01",
            {"incident_id": param("string"), "comment_id": param("string"),
             "message": param("string", maxLength=8000)},
            {"created": {"type": "string"}}, {"created": "$.properties.createdTimeUtc"},
            risk="low", effect="mutating",
            body={"properties": {"message": "{{ inputs.message }}"}}),
    ],
)
sentinel["poll"] = {"command": "sentinel.list_incidents",
                    "watermark_field": "properties.lastModifiedTimeUtc",
                    "interval_s": 60}

splunk = connector(
    "splunk.enterprise_security", "Splunk Enterprise Security", "Splunk", "siem",
    {"kind": "api_key", "roles": ["token"], "header": "Authorization",
     "prefix": "Bearer "},
    "{{ integration.config.base_url }}",
    ["{{ integration.config.host }}"],
    min_permissions=["search", "edit_notable_events"],
    health={"path": "/services/server/info?output_mode=json"},
    setup=[
        field("base_url", "Splunk API URL", kind="url",
              placeholder="https://splunk.client.example:8089",
              help="The management port, not the web UI on 8000."),
        field("index", "Index to search", required=False,
              placeholder="notable"),
        field("app", "App context", required=False,
              placeholder="SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite"),
    ],
    hunt={
        "command": "splunk.run_search", "input": "search",
        "output": "rows", "language": "SPL",
        "window_input": "earliest_time", "window_format": "-{hours}h",
    },
    commands=[
        cmd("splunk.run_search", "Splunk: Run Search", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/services/search/jobs/export?output_mode=json",
            {"search": param("string", maxLength=32768),
             "earliest_time": param("string"), "latest_time": param("string")},
            rows_out, required=["search"], timeout_ms=180000,
            body={"search": "{{ inputs.search }}",
                  "earliest_time": "{{ inputs.earliest_time | default('-24h') }}",
                  "latest_time": "{{ inputs.latest_time | default('now') }}"},
            doc="SPL as a parameter. The same rule as KQL: saved or approved, "
                "never assembled from alert fields."),

        cmd("splunk.get_notables", "Splunk: Get Notable Events", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/services/search/jobs/export?output_mode=json",
            {"since": param("string")},
            {"notables": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            required=[],
            body={"search": "search `notable` | where _time > relative_time(now(), \"{{ inputs.since | default('-5m') }}\")"},
            doc="The polling command for notable-event ingestion."),

        cmd("splunk.update_notable", "Splunk: Update Notable Event", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/services/notable_update",
            {"event_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
             "status": param("integer", enum=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]),
             "comment": param("string")},
            {"success": {"type": "boolean"}}, {"success": "$.success"},
            risk="medium", effect="mutating", required=["event_ids", "status"],
            body={"ruleUIDs": "{{ inputs.event_ids | json }}",
                  "status": "{{ inputs.status }}",
                  "comment": "{{ inputs.comment }}"}),
    ],
)
splunk["poll"] = {"command": "splunk.get_notables",
                  "watermark_field": "_time", "interval_s": 60}

qradar = connector(
    "ibm.qradar", "IBM QRadar", "IBM", "siem",
    {"kind": "api_key", "roles": ["sec_token"], "header": "SEC"},
    "{{ integration.config.base_url }}",
    ["{{ integration.config.host }}"],
    min_permissions=["Offenses read", "Offenses close"],
    health={"path": "/api/system/about"},
    setup=[
        field("base_url", "Console URL", kind="url",
              placeholder="https://qradar.client.example"),
        field("api_version", "API version", required=False,
              placeholder="20.0",
              help="QRadar changes response shapes between versions; pin it if you have had a surprise."),
    ],
    hunt={
        "command": "qradar.run_aql", "input": "query",
        "output": "search_id", "language": "AQL",
        # AQL searches are asynchronous: this returns a search id and
        # the results are collected on a second call, so a QRadar hunt
        # records the handle rather than the rows.
        "deferred": True,
    },
    commands=[
        cmd("qradar.list_offenses", "QRadar: List Offenses", "GET",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/api/siem/offenses?filter={{ inputs.filter | urlencode }}",
            {"filter": param("string")},
            {"offenses": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            required=[]),

        cmd("qradar.get_offense", "QRadar: Get Offense", "GET",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/api/siem/offenses/{{ inputs.offense_id | urlencode }}",
            {"offense_id": param("string")},
            {"description": {"type": "string"}, "magnitude": {"type": "integer"},
             "status": {"type": "string"}}),

        cmd("qradar.run_aql", "QRadar: Run AQL Search", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/api/ariel/searches?query_expression={{ inputs.query | urlencode }}",
            {"query": param("string", maxLength=16384)},
            {"search_id": {"type": "string"}}, {"search_id": "$.search_id"},
            timeout_ms=180000),

        cmd("qradar.close_offense", "QRadar: Close Offense", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/api/siem/offenses/{{ inputs.offense_id | urlencode }}?status=CLOSED&closing_reason_id={{ inputs.reason_id }}",
            {"offense_id": param("string"), "reason_id": param("integer")},
            {"status": {"type": "string"}},
            risk="medium", effect="mutating"),
    ],
)
qradar["poll"] = {"command": "qradar.list_offenses",
                  "watermark_field": "last_updated_time", "interval_s": 60}

elastic = connector(
    "elastic.security", "Elastic Security", "Elastic", "siem",
    {"kind": "api_key", "roles": ["api_key"], "header": "Authorization",
     "prefix": "ApiKey "},
    "{{ integration.config.base_url }}",
    ["{{ integration.config.host }}"],
    health={"path": "/_cluster/health"},
    setup=[
        field("base_url", "Elasticsearch URL", kind="url",
              placeholder="https://deployment.es.region.cloud.es.io:9243",
              help="The Elasticsearch endpoint, not the Kibana one."),
        field("kibana_url", "Kibana URL", kind="url", required=False,
              help="Needed for detection-rule and case commands."),
        field("space", "Kibana space", required=False,
              placeholder="default"),
    ],
    hunt={
        "command": "elastic.run_query", "input": "query",
        "output": "rows", "language": "ES|QL",
        # ES|QL carries its own time filter in the query text, so there
        # is no window parameter to hand it.
    },
    commands=[
        cmd("elastic.run_query", "Elastic: Run ES|QL Query", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/_query?format=json",
            {"query": param("string", maxLength=16384)},
            rows_out, {"rows": "$.values"}, timeout_ms=120000,
            body={"query": "{{ inputs.query }}"}),

        cmd("elastic.get_alerts", "Elastic: Get Detection Alerts", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.base_url }}/api/detection_engine/signals/search",
            {"since": param("string")},
            {"alerts": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"alerts": "$.hits.hits"}, required=[],
            body={"query": {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "{{ inputs.since | default('now-5m') }}"}}}}),
    ],
)
elastic["poll"] = {"command": "elastic.get_alerts",
                   "watermark_field": "@timestamp", "interval_s": 60}

return [sentinel, splunk, qradar, elastic]
